scope: Reentrant changes within the same preference binding after destination notifications.

red.behavior: Newer same-binding state remained in memory but old setter/hydration/reset persisted old values;old setters could overwrite pending newer values.

targeted.note: Before one additional explicit user-reset contract case;final contract run and full suite cover that case.

behavior: Persist/apply the post-notification current accessibility snapshot rather than merging the old patch back over it.
Queue only setter leaves whose value still matches after notification;unrelated newer leaves and still-owned outer leaves both survive.
Time-format setter/hydration/reset persist current state;superseded setter value is not queued.
Strengthened account/backend cases directly assert the one surviving persisted pending queue and exact replacement patch.
Explicit user reset preserves a newer leaf while queueing unaffected default leaves.
limits: Real synchronous Zustand/destination/preferences behavior with no-op bootstrap presentation;not real browser authentication/native/provider acceptance.
Other destination methods and whole RF13/offline/native/physical/project acceptance remain open.
No claim that general event backpressure or active search unique-ID memory frontier is complete.
